transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-05-27 09:00 PT | Duration: ~75 minutes | Attendees: Olivia Chen, Marcus Patel, Ava Rodriguez, Samir Khan, Priya Desai, Noah Williams, Lena Park, Ethan Moore

Summary: quick sync on Q3 roadmap and launch readiness for Dedicated release. go over the incident last week, make sure canary and autoscale are solid. assign owners for runbooks, benchmarks, and regression evals.

Topics: Q3 roadmap priorities; Launch readiness checklist; Incident review 2026-05-20; Autoscaling/Dedicated capacity; VPC/KMS and quantization testing

00:00:12 Olivia: okay, let's start, um — thanks everyone for joining, I know this is the pre-weekend sync so we'll try to keep it tight. first item, q3 milestones. ava you want to kick off?
00:00:28 Ava: sure, quick overview — we have feature freeze in two weeks, GA target 2026-06-22, internally we're calling it dedicated-v2 launch. primary goals: stable p95 under 200ms for 8k context on Dedicated pools, rollout path for canary -> 10% -> 50% -> GA; and audit logs + KMS integration for customers.
00:00:52 Marcus: right, and engineering wise we need the autoscaler tuning done, the kernel selection fallback in place for long sequences, and the KV cache eviction policy tested under churn.
00:01:10 Priya: on KV cache, the last test showed cache thrash at high concurrency, we saw increased tail latencies when prefixes were misaligned, that might be connected to the 05-20 incident.
00:01:28 Samir: yeah i'll dig into the runbook notes — quick recap for anyone missed it: on 2026-05-20 after the midnight deploy we saw a latency spike, p99 went up to ~2.8s for like 12 minutes, autoscale didn't react fast enough due to threshold configs and a metric aggregation delay.
00:01:48 Noah: and we also had a partial rollback which caused some config drift — the canary didn't fully validate the quantized model variant because the eval set was incomplete.
00:02:05 Olivia: that points to two things: improve canary criteria + fix autoscaling thresholds and detection window. what are concrete fixes?
00:02:18 Marcus: for autoscale, short term we can lower the aggregation window to 30s and add a ramp up policy for dedicated pools. long term we want predictive scaling based on request rate and prefix patterns. but the immediate change is config.
00:02:36 Ava: add to action items: lock the lower aggregation window and document it. lena can you handle GA freeze coordination?
00:02:45 Lena: yes i'll schedule the freeze window, propose 2026-06-08 to 2026-06-22 as the no-large-change window, with emergency exception process documented.
00:02:58 Ethan: note about networking — VPC peering and KMS rotations need to be tested in staging, if the KMS key policy changes during the freeze it could break deployments. so suggest a key holdback test.
00:03:16 Priya: ok for the benchmark, i'll run the dedicated-pool load test (1M tokens/day equivalent) in staging next week and capture p50/p95/p99 and cost profiles. i'll include quantized and non-quantized variants.
00:03:33 Olivia: perfect. on regression evals, noah you said the eval set was incomplete? what's missing?
00:03:41 Noah: we don't have enough long-context prompts and streaming edge cases; also the hallucination checks for structured outputs are sparse. i'll expand the eval to include 10 long-guidance prompts and some streaming scenarios.
00:03:56 Marcus: related to models, compilation/kernel selection fallback needs to prefer stable kernels for long sequences; we've seen newer kernels degrade on certain llama variants. add that to the ops checklist.
00:04:12 Ava: let's talk timeline. feature freeze 2026-06-08? we just set that as the freeze window start. freeze means no infra changes except security hotfixes.
00:04:24 Samir: correct. and we should have full disaster recovery drill before freeze ends. runbook: step-by-step rollback, golden images, ip whitelisting rollback. i'll update the runbook tonight and share.
00:04:38 Olivia: good. next, incident review detail — samir can you walk the timeline from 05-20?
00:04:46 Samir: yep, timeline: 00:15 deploy started, 00:42 anomaly detection flagged increased latency, 00:48 we hit p99 spike, 00:52 autoscaler started adding nodes but it was slow — by 01:04 latency subsided after partial rollback and manual scaling. root cause: metric aggregation delay + canary not exercising quantized path. secondary cause: KV cache eviction thrash.
00:05:10 Priya: small correction, the KV thrash was due to a config mismatch between staging and prod — the eviction TTL in staging was higher which masked it. so we need config parity checks.
00:05:24 Marcus: add to action items: config parity test during CI; maybe a lint step that compares key infra flags.
00:05:32 Ava: also, we should define canary pass/fail criteria more strictly — include p95 threshold, error spike threshold, and end-to-end smoke test that hits both quantized and non-quantized code paths.
00:05:49 Noah: i'll implement the smoke tests; they need to run in canary and report to the canary dashboard. currently the dashboard only checks a small set of endpoints.
00:06:03 Olivia: good. switching to observability: what gaps in monitoring do we have? samir?
00:06:09 Samir: we need token-level tracing for cost attribution (that's on the roadmap) but immediate need is better per-route latency breakdown, plus trace sampling for high-concurrency flows. also alerting thresholds need different bands for Dedicated vs Hosted.
00:06:27 Marcus: agree — we've had alert noise where Hosted thresholds were used for Dedicated, causing unnecessary paging. fix is a route-level policy and default override per deployment type.
00:06:40 Ava: for release, we need an ops checklist: runbook updated, monitoring tuned, canary test plan, benchmark results, security sign-off (SOC2/ISO doc updates), and customer docs.
00:06:56 Ethan: on security, KMS integration test plan should include key rotation simulation and verifying audit logs. compliance wants proof of audit logs across the release window.
00:07:08 Olivia: ok let's capture owners again for those checklist items.
00:07:12 (brief crosstalk)
00:07:28 Olivia: samir, runbook. priya, benchmarks. noah, regression/ smoke tests. lena, freeze window and release coordination. marcus, autoscale and kernel fallback. ava, roadmap finalization. is that right?
00:07:44 All: yes/ack.
00:07:55 Priya: quick Q — for benchmarks, do we use the real dataset or synthetic? synthetic gives more repeatability but real traffic is desirable.
00:08:04 Marcus: do both; synthetic for repeatability, and a sampled real-traffic replay for more realistic prefix distributions. make sure to include prefix alignment tests to expose KV thrash.
00:08:19 Noah: another note — quantization regressions can be subtle, so add a human review on failed evals for edge cases.
00:08:29 Ava: timeline check: priya benchmark 2026-06-02, noah regression set by 2026-05-31, samir runbook by 2026-06-03, ava lock dates by 2026-06-01. we'll call out to stakeholders once done.
00:08:44 Marcus: also need to confirm Dedicated capacity commits — finance needs projected utilization to size pools. priya can include cost per token in the benchmark output.
00:08:56 Priya: will do.
00:09:02 Olivia: move on to rollout strategy — canary -> 10% -> 50% -> GA? how long each step?
00:09:10 Lena: propose canary 24h, 10% 48h, 50% 72h with metric gates at each step; if regression evals or smoke tests fail we rollback.
00:09:24 Marcus: add automatic fallback to hosted-compatible model variant if Dedicated kernel fails; that keeps customer-facing apps online, degrade gracefully.
00:09:36 Samir: ops note: implement circuit breaker that routes to hosted model pool for a specific tenant if p99 exceeds threshold for more than 3 minutes.
00:09:49 Olivia: good fail-safe. any other infra blockers?
00:09:53 Ethan: VPC egress rules for some customers need confirmation — one customer uses strict firewalling which broke our telemetry collection in sandbox last month. coordinate with customer ops for allowlist.
00:10:06 Priya: that's in the customer onboarding checklist but good point, lena please surface that when scheduling pre-GA customer comms.
00:10:15 Olivia: ok let's do the incident post-mortem notes quickly — root cause, remediation, preventative actions. samir?
00:10:23 Samir: root cause: metric aggregation delay + canary coverage gap. remediation: lower aggregation window, update canary tests, roll runbook changes. preventative: CI config parity checks, benchmark + regression gate before deploy.
00:10:41 Noah: also recommend adding smoke tests that exercise quantized path specifically. add human review for critical regression failures.
00:10:50 Marcus: and a load test that simulates prefix churn at scale to expose cache eviction behavior.
00:10:58 Ava: noted. any blockers for implementing these within the freeze window?
00:11:04 Priya: we need staging infra to allocate time on Dedicated pools for the benchmark, but we can schedule next Tue. I'll coordinate with infra.
00:11:14 Ethan: infra can provide a 12-hour window on Tue for the replay. need a ticket to reserve.
00:11:21 Priya: i'll create the ticket after the call.
00:11:25 Olivia: excellent. switching briefly to docs and customer comms — compliance artifacts for SOC2 and KMS need updates. who's owning that?
00:11:33 Lena: Security will own final sign-off but i'll collect the checklist items and ensure the required docs are attached to the release PR.
00:11:41 Marcus: re: kernel selection, will engineering add a fallback layer that prefers stable kernels? we had a build that picked an experimental kernel by default.
00:11:50 Priya: we can pin kernel versions in staging and add an integration test that runs a small long-context job to compare.
00:11:58 Olivia: ok. last 10 minutes let's do a quick run through of the launch readiness checklist and owners.
00:12:06 (fast recap, people enumerate items)
00:12:22 Olivia: runbook? samir. benchmark? priya. regression and smoke tests? noah. freeze scheduling? lena. autoscale + kernel fallback? marcus. roadmap finalization and stakeholder comms? ava. finance utilization numbers? marcus and priya. anything else?
00:12:39 Marcus: one more infra note — we should add a rollback-of-rollback plan, because last time the partial rollback left config drift. ensure rollback is atomic where possible.
00:12:50 Samir: will include atomic rollback checklist in runbook.
00:12:57 Ava: ok i'm going to send the updated roadmap doc after this. expect a follow-up email with the finalized dates and an invite for the DR drill.
00:13:08 Olivia: nice. any open questions?
00:13:12 Priya: quick one — do we want to run quantization A/B against a small set of customers before GA?
00:13:19 Lena: we have capacity to do a targeted pilot, but legal/compliance needs signoff for any customer-facing A/B. plan that as a separate pilot request.
00:13:31 Olivia: wrap up — we'll reconvene next Tuesday post-benchmark to review numbers. thanks everyone.
00:13:38 (meeting ends)

Recap & explicit next steps:
- Samir: update runbook with post-mortem + atomic rollback checklist; due 2026-06-03.
- Priya: run dedicated-pool benchmark (synthetic + replay) and share p50/p95/p99 + cost; due 2026-06-02.
- Noah: expand regression evals and add smoke tests for quantized/non-quantized paths; due 2026-05-31.
- Ava: finalize roadmap dates and stakeholder sign-off; due 2026-06-01.
- Marcus: lock autoscale defaults and kernel fallback plan; due 2026-06-04.
- Lena: schedule freeze window and coordinate customer communication; due 2026-06-08.
